layout_note: Single column, roman body type (the 'direction of the reader' face). This section occupies the LOWER HALF of page 20; the UPPER HALF is the tail end of the PREVIOUS section, 'THE ARGVMENT OF GENESIS' (whose centered running header this page carries, and whose left-margin apparatus 'This booke diuided into eight partes.' + numerals 1-8 belong to that Argument, NOT to this section -- so they are excluded here). The marks section is a two-line centered display heading followed by a hanging-indent LIST of nine entries, each explaining one reference mark/symbol used in the margins and text of the Bible. Printed mark-glyphs appear inline: a cross in brackets [+], a raised double-comma/prime annotation mark (rendered here as U+2033 double-prime), four pricks (rendered as two colons ::), and a starre in brackets [*]. Page is UNPAGINATED (front matter); pagination begins on the next leaf (page_index 21 = folio 'I', start of 'THE BOOKE OF GENESIS ... CHAP. I'), which is where this section ENDS -- the biblical text begins there. Full jp2 raster is 3334x4684 px (native, highest raster); raster_dpi 400 recorded per pipeline convention. Glyph regime is uniform roman body prose: lowercase w is a real connected w-sort; the only vv is the word-initial capital 'VVe' (entry 9), a genuine gapped two-V sort (this fount's capital W).

body.text: The ſignification of the markes here vſed, for
direction of the reader.
The numbers in the argumentes of chapters point to the verſe, where the mat-
ter mentioned beginneth.
This forme of croſſe [†] in the text, sheweth the beginning of euerie verſe.
The numbers in the inner margent ouer againſt the croſſes, shew the number
of verſes in the ſame chapter.
This marke ″ ſignifieth that there foloweth an Annotation after the chapter,
vpon the word, or wordes, wherto it is adioyned. The number alſo of the
ſame verſe is prefixed to the Annotation.
Theſe foure prickes :: shew that there is an Annotation in the margent, vpon
that place. And when manie occurre, the firſt anſwereth to the firſt marcke,
the ſecond to the ſecond, and ſo forth. In like maner the citations of places
in the inner margent, are applied to the authores alleaged.
But when there be more ſuch marginal annotations, then may eaſely be ap-
plied, we vſe the letters of the Alphabete for direction.
This forme of a ſtarre [*] in the text or annotations, pointeth to the explica-
tion of ſome word or wordes, in the margent.
Sometimes we put the Concordance of other Scriptures in the inner mar-
gent of the text.
VVe haue alſo noted in the margent, when the Bookes of holie Scripture (or
partes thereof) are read in the Churches Seruice. For their ſakes, that deſire
to read the ſame, in order of the Eccleſiaſtical Office.

uncertain.note: TWO items on this line. (1) A stray raised point appears between 'anſwereth' and 'to' on the plate ('anſwereth .to'); it is almost certainly a broken/errant point or ink speck (no grammatical role mid-clause) and has been OMITTED from the canonical text. Confidence high that it is an artifact, not intended punctuation. (2) 'marcke' -- verified letter-by-letter at high zoom as m-a-r-c-k-e; this is a same-page SPELLING VARIANT of 'marke' (the heading and entry idx 4 both spell it 'marke'). Preserved diplomatically as printed, NOT normalized. High confidence in the reading.

Round-s vs long-ſ call (glyph-driven per §long-ſ). Verified at 3x zoom: the initial s of 'sheweth' is a SHORT/round s (no descender) -> 'sheweth' (round s + h), NOT 'ſheweth'. Same call for 'shew' at line_index 5 and line_index 10 (both round-s). Consistent with the guideline warning against over-producing ſ in sh-clusters.

'letters' verified l-e-t-t-e-r-s at zoom (the medial 'r' is worn and can read as a stray 't' -> 'lettets' in raw OCR; resolved to 'letters'). 'vſe' = v + long-ſ + e (u/v swap for 'use'); the v can read as 'r' at low res. Both resolved high confidence.

Comma spacing: 'verſe,where' is set tight on the plate (little/no space after the comma). Rendered with a normal following space here; the §French-spacing rule concerns space BEFORE high punctuation (: ; ? !), not commas, so the tight comma is treated as ordinary compositor spacing, not a diplomatic feature. Low significance.

w-vs-vv call (§w-regime). Word-initial capital verified at zoom as a GAPPED two-V sort (VV), i.e. this fount's capital-W = genuine 'VV'. Transcribed 'VVe'. All LOWERCASE body w on the page (sheweth, shew, when, we, word(es), wherto, foloweth, anſwereth) are real connected w-sorts -> 'w'. High confidence.

method: Visual multimodal read of the native jp2 full-page raster (archive-ot1-1609 page_index 20, S1) plus targeted 2-3x crops for every ambiguous glyph. FOUR VALIDATIONS: (1) LOCALIZATION -- PASS: heading reads 'The ſignification of the markes here vſed, for direction of the reader.' and the nine entries explain exactly the reference marks (cross [†], four-pricks ::, double-prime ″, starre [*], chapter-argument numbers, marginal-verse numbers, alphabet letters, concordance, liturgical notes); this is the marks-legend, not a lookalike. (2) IDENTITY -- PASS: 1609 OT1 First Tome (S1), the same volume as the Duaci-1609 Approbatio; the following leaf (page_index 21) is folio 'I' opening 'THE BOOKE OF GENESIS, IN HEBREW BERESITH. CHAP. I', confirming this is the OT1 1609 front matter immediately before Genesis. (3) PLACEMENT -- PASS: page is unpaginated front matter; centered running header 'THE ARGVMENT OF GENESIS.'; section sits in the lower half of page 20, directly after the tail of the Argument of Genesis (upper half) and directly before Genesis 1 (page 21). (4) COMPLETENESS -- PASS: the ENTIRE section is on page 20; it does NOT continue onto page 21 (which begins the biblical text of Genesis 1). No catchword or quire-signature at the foot of page 20 (blank below 'Office.'). All 23 physical lines transcribed; no lines dropped. Reference DR consulted for content-anchor only; no modern spelling copied.
confidence: high on the whole section (roman body prose, clean impression). Glyph-level calls verified at zoom: sheweth/shew/shew = round-s; croſſe/croſſes = long-ſſ; VVe = gapped capital VV; marcke = same-page variant of marke (preserved). Only minor flag: a stray raised point in 'anſwereth .to' (line 11) judged an artifact and omitted.
glyph_regime_resolved: Uniform roman BODY prose (the 'direction of the reader' face) -- NOT the annotation/footnote face, so no vv-substitution regime applies to lowercase. Lowercase w = real connected w-sort throughout (sheweth, shew, when, we, word/wordes, wherto, foloweth, anſwereth). The single vv is the word-initial CAPITAL 'VVe' (entry 9), a genuine gapped two-V sort = this fount's capital W (per §w-regime priors: genuine vv clusters at word-initial capitals). long-ſ is glyph-driven and mixed: sh-clusters (sheweth, shew) verified round-s; ſt/ſſ/medial-ſ verified long-ſ (againſt, croſſe, firſt, ſecond, etc.). u/v period-swap preserved (vſed, vpon, ouer, euerie, haue, Seruice, vſe). i/j preserved (adioyned). ct-ligatures transcribed as components (direction). Archaic spellings preserved (argumentes, foloweth, wherto, eaſely, maner, occurre, authores, alleaged, margent, holie, partes, Seruice, Eccleſiaſtical, Alphabete, marcke). Printed mark glyphs kept in archaic text: [†], ″, ::, [*].
